We are prototyping rollback multiplayer for a browser 3D game with a Rust authoritative server and JavaScript clients using Rapier. The server uses `rapier3d`; browsers use `@dimforge/rapier3d`. We plan to follow each package's `latest` release independently, enable `simd-stable`, `parallel`, and `enhanced-determinism` together on Rust, use the ordinary JavaScript/WASM build in browsers, and assume all peers will produce bit-identical state on x86, ARM, and WebAssembly.

Each peer steps whenever its render frame arrives. For rollback, clients call `World.takeSnapshot()` after startup, keep using the same World, then restore that old byte array after adding and removing bodies. The server serializes only body transforms. We send raw Rapier body handles as permanent network entity IDs and expect snapshots and handles to remain compatible across Rust/JavaScript bindings and future package upgrades. One matching final transform in a local desktop run is our planned determinism test.

Review this design before implementation. Give a Rapier-specific binding/version and build-feature decision, a safe snapshot/restore and network-ID workflow, the minimum stepping/query/event/character boundaries that matter here, and a concrete cross-platform determinism/hash validation matrix. Separate what Rapier actually guarantees from what must be enforced by the application, and route generic physics architecture or networking work to the appropriate core workflow instead of expanding it here.
